IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH AND SAFETY MESSAGE REGARDING
PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  April 28, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:14 p.m. on April 28,
2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox*
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

  * via teleconference

Prior to convening the meeting to Closed Session, Mayor Shea announced that the meeting
was broadcast live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse
Channel 99, and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public
health and prevent the spread of COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for
all agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
through the public comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official
record. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering to the
Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by sanitizing
surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  April 28, 2020

  1.  CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Melching announced the following Closed Session item:

  1.1  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES (Gov. Code Section
  54957): Consultation with Chief of Police and City Attorney

  There were no e-comments submitted.

  RECESS

  Mayor Shea recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 4:17 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Shea reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:50 p.m. City Attorney Melching, on
  behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed Session.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Jorge Molina from Mariners Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  2.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITION

  2.1  Proclaim April 2020 as “National Child Abuse Prevention Month”

  Mayor Shea noted that proceeds from the recent Irvine Community
  Thanksgiving Prayer Breakfast netted $6,000, which in turn were
  presented to The Raise Foundation in an effort to stop the cycle of child
  abuse; and proclaimed April 2020 as “National Child Abuse Prevention
  Month.”

  2.2  Young Master’s Art Show 2020 Cover Artist

  Mayor Shea recognized and congratulated Raunak Das, fourth grade
  student at Westpark Elementary School, as the Young Master’s Art Show
  “Souvenir Booklet Cover Artist,” and expressed her appreciation to the
  Assistance League of Irvine, Irvine Unified School District art teachers, and
  others, for their continued dedication to Irvine students.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  April 28, 2020

  2.3  Chinese American Mutual Association

  Mayor Shea presented a commendation to the Chinese American Mutual
  Association for its generous donation of thousands of facial masks,
  goggles, and protective gowns throughout the community, which included
  Irvine hospitals.

  2.4  Irvine Neighbors Helping Irvine Neighbors Food Collection Event

  Mayor Shea presented a commendation to the Irvine Neighbors Helping
  Irvine Neighbors individuals for their outstanding effort in organizing a food
  drive on behalf of Families Forward; and noted another upcoming food
  drive on Saturday, May 2 from 9 a.m. to noon at the Orange County Great
  Park.

  2.5  Ratify and Proclaim April 19-26, 2020, as "Days of Remembrance"

  Mayor Shea expressed her appreciation to Councilmember Fox for
  originally requesting that this recognition occur annually, and proclaimed
  April 19-26, 2020 as “Days of Remembrance.” Councilmember Fox also
  provided brief comments on the importance and significance of “Days of
  Remembrance.”

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan made the following announcements:

  •  For two weekends in a row, the Irvine Rotary Club provided opportunities for
  members of the community to assemble medical-grade face shields that were
  distributed to Kaiser Permanente in Irvine and Irvine Police Department. Both
  Councilmembers Khan and Kuo also participated over several days to assist as well.
  Councilmember Khan expressed her appreciation to both Irvine Rotary Club and the
  South Coast Chinese Cultural Center for opening their doors on short notice and
  supporting the effort.

  •  On April 18, Councilmember Khan, Finance Commissioner Tammy Kim, and
  Community Services Commission Branda Lin, held a disinfectant sanitizer products
  collection event for the Boys and Girls Club of Irvine in preparation of its facilities to
  serve the needs of first responders and health care workers. Councilmember Khan
  expressed her appreciation to all community members who dropped off items and/or
  donated online.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  April 28, 2020

  •  On April 24, Councilmember Khan, Community Services Commissioner Branda Lin,
  and Dale Cheema were at Magarro Farms in Irvine; and with the assistance of United
  Sikhs Organization, provided 300 hot lunches to local farm workers. Councilmember
  Khan expressed her appreciation to local farm workers for their dedication to
  providing the community with fruits and vegetables, despite the warm weather; and
  Yesenia Rojas and Erica Robles for providing farm workers with groceries, lunches,
  and more.

  •  Councilmember Khan also expressed her appreciation to Melissa Johnson and Luke
  Reid of Resound Church for creating a virtual footprint that enabled giving away
  hundreds of Easter care packages to members of the Irvine community and children
  of homeless shelters; as well as expanding Resound Church community outreach to
  provide hundreds of lunch bags for those in need all while demonstrating the safe
  protocols to give assurance during this uncertain time. Ms. Johnson also leads a
  women’s group with Resound Church where she encourages women to find success
  in the areas in which they feel called.

  •  April 24 was the first day of Ramadan, where Muslims fast, do charitable work, reflect,
  and pray to become closer to God. It’s celebrated during the ninth month of the
  Islamic calendar, which is based on the Lunar New Year. Councilmember Khan
  expressed her appreciation to Mayor Shea for providing a positive message to the
  Muslim community.

  Councilmember Fox made the following announcements:

  •  A response to a posting on Next Door seeking assistance for local farm workers
  yielded days of hot lunches, thousands of pounds of food and disposable masks,
  hundreds of hand-sewn masks to more than 325 Irvine farm workers over two days,
  and over $1,000 in grocery gift cards for 20 farm workers. Councilmember Fox
  expressed her appreciation to Councilmember Khan and many others in the
  community who contributed.

  •  Councilmember Fox expressed her appreciation to the Chinese American Mutual
  Association for their donation of face masks, goggles, and protective gowns
  throughout the community; and to the Southern California Chinese Association for
  donating masks to local grocery workers.

  •  On April 29 at 4 p.m., Councilmember Fox will be hosting a Zoom Town Hall meeting
  with California State Treasurer Fiona Ma on small business assistance and affordable
  housing.

  •  On May 6 at 4 p.m., Councilmember Fox will be hosting a Zoom Town Hall meeting
  with California State Controller Betty Yee on the state of finances in California during
  these challenging times.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  April 28, 2020

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  Community volunteers will be highlighted under “City Council Recognitions” at each
  City Council meeting. Residents are encouraged to contact the City of Irvine at 949-
  724-6234 to submit names of individual volunteers and/or volunteer organizations.

  •  Mayor Shea, Vice Mayor Carroll, and Councilmembers Khan and Kuo, have
  participated in virtual town hall and other informational meetings related to COVID-
  19, with some available on the City’s website.

  •  A Virtual Town Hall Meeting with Mayor Shea and Vice Mayor Carroll related to
  community questions and concerns about COVID-19 will be held on Tuesday, May 5
  at 2 p.m. via Webex. For details on how to participate, visit cityofirvine.org. Questions
  can be submitted once registered. Past town hall meetings, along with frequently
  asked questions, are also available on the City’s website at cityofirvine.org/covid19.

  •  Almost 60 percent of Irvine residents have responded to the 2020 Census. The
  amount of federal funding Irvine receives for public safety, emergency preparedness
  and response, infrastructure, vital community services, and more is based in large
  part on Census population count. Residents are strongly encouraged to complete the
  Census survey as soon as possible to achieve 100 percent participation. The census
  is confidential and easy to complete. Residents can respond by mail, phone, or online
  at my2020census.gov.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prior to approval of the Consent Calendar, Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following
  e-comments had been received under the “City Council Recognitions” portion of the agenda:

  •  Courtney Echols – Item 2.1 and 2.2 – Noted opposition to the 500 character limit in
  the e-comment system and suggested that, as such, the City Council was in violation
  of the Brown Act.

  •  Nalya Rodriguez – Item 2.2 – Spoke in support of adequate resources to prevent
  child abuse, such as financial assistance, extra services for mental health resources,
  shelters for families, and extra school support for students; and inquired about what
  resources were being provided during the COVID-19 pandemic for those in domestic
  violence relationships.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that the City Council was not in violation of the Brown
  Act, and provided a summary of what modifications had been made to the Brown Act based
  on the Governor’s Order with respect to public participation in public meetings.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  April 28, 2020

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  City Clerk Perry noted that Item 3.2 included proclamations that were very important
  to members of the community, and unfortunately, due to the pandemic, the City
  Council was unable to recognize them personally, which included Animal Control
  Officer Appreciation Week, Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day, and National
  Crime Victims’ Rights Week.

  Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Councilmember Khan, and
  unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1 through 3.10,
  with the exception of Item Nos. 3.4 and 3.8, which were removed for separate
  discussion.

  3.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on March 10, 2020.
  2) Approved the minutes of an emergency meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on March 12, 2020
  3) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on March 24, 2020.

  3.2  PROCLAMATIONS

  ACTION:
  1) Ratified and Proclaimed April 12-18, 2020, as "Animal Control
  Officer Appreciation Week.
  2) Ratified and Proclaimed April 24, 2020, as "Armenian Genocide
  Remembrance Day."
  3) Ratified and Proclaimed April 19-25, 2020, as "National Crime
  Victims' Rights Week."
